articles.title: Letter: Support the Senior Exercise Class
body: To the editor: Thank you for printing this letter, and for all the work the paper does to keep us informed. To the editor: I have lived on Fox Terrace for 25 years, and I want to say what a difference the Marsh Landing Pond Committee has made.
Please keep the senior exercise class in the budget. Many of us on Fox Terrace use it every week. I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the November meeting.
Keith Kellerman, Foundry Row

articles.title: Council Tables Sidewalk Ramp Ordinance
articles.deck: The vote came after 39 residents spoke at Wednesday’s session.
body: Councilmember Hannah Sandoval asked for more time to review the proposal, which would cost about $48,000. Residents of Eastgate said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

The ordinance will return to the agenda at the next regular session, unless the chair calls a special meeting first. Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.

articles.title: Then & Now: Mulberry Avenue in 1985 and Today
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.

A 1985 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Mulberry Avenue from the corner of Carver Drive. Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal.

articles.title: The Upper Commons Historical Society Plans Bus Shelter for Summer
articles.deck: Residents of Hickory Ridge met on Wednesday to talk over the plan.
body: The Hickory Ridge Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library. The effort began in February when a handful of neighbors met at the Foundry Row fire house to talk about bus shelter.
Several residents on Carver Drive said they had been waiting since 1992 for something like this. The group has raised $25,000 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food.

Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Foundry Row fire house on Wednesday at 7 p.m. Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Wednesday mornings.
